short: A son of the Conqueror who reunited England and Normandy under a single crown.
full:
Henry I seized the English throne in August 1100 immediately following the sudden death of his brother William II. He issued a Charter of Liberties to appease the barons and married Matilda of Scotland, binding the Norman dynasty to the old Anglo-Saxon royal line. In 1106, he decisively defeated his eldest brother, Robert Curthose, at the Battle of Tinchebray, reuniting the territories divided at their father's death.

Henry constructed a sophisticated bureaucracy, establishing the Exchequer to manage royal revenues and deploying itinerant justices to project royal authority across the shires. Despite his administrative success and holding power for thirty-five years, his reign ended in a succession crisis. The death of his only legitimate son in 1120 left his daughter Matilda as heir, a controversial choice that triggered a devastating civil war upon his death.
